name: quantumtrace-vscode
description: Highlights quantum-vulnerable cryptography in Python, Java and Go, explains the risk, says what to migrate to, and shows which of it your tests really run.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted workspace QuantumTrace ignores workspace settings that choose which command to run or where to send code.

quantumtrace.backend.description: How the extension reaches the QuantumTrace engine.

quantumtrace.cli.command.markdownDescription: Command that starts the QuantumTrace CLI, one item per argument. Use absolute paths, for example `["uv", "run", "--project", "/path/to/backend", "quantumtrace"]`.

quantumtrace.api.url.markdownDescription: Base URL of the QuantumTrace API, for example `http://localhost:8000`. Leave empty to use the API this copy of the extension was built for, if any.

quantumtrace.scanOnSave.description: Scan Python, Java and Go files when they are opened or saved.

quantumtrace.scanOnType.markdownDescription: Scan a file again a moment after you stop typing, without saving it. Only the local QuantumTrace CLI does this, so unsaved text never leaves this machine; through the API, files are scanned when saved. Has no effect when `quantumtrace.scanOnSave` is off.

quantumtrace.trace.command.markdownDescription: The command **QuantumTrace: Run tests with the runtime tracer** runs in the workspace folder, one item per argument. It must start Python 3.12 or newer. A leading `python` becomes the interpreter the Python extension has selected, if that extension is installed.

quantumtrace.trace.debugSessions.description: Also trace the Python debug sessions you start in VS Code, so a debug run shows what it executed too.

enumDescriptions: Underline the call, and list every finding in the Problems panel.
quantumtrace.style.description: How findings are marked in the editor.

enumDescriptions: Red, so Shor-vulnerable code stands apart from Grover-weakened code.
Yellow, the same as Grover-weakened code.
quantumtrace.criticalSeverity.description: Colour of Shor-vulnerable (critical) findings. Grover-weakened (medium) findings are always yellow.

quantumtrace.explainOnClick.description: Open the explanation when you click a marked finding.

quantumtrace.inlineHint.description: Show a few words after each marked line saying what is wrong with it.

quantumtrace.codeLens.description: After a traced run, show above each marked line that ran how often it ran and in which test.

quantumtrace.aiFix.markdownDescription: Offer **Fix with AI** on each finding. It asks before sending anything: the file goes to the QuantumTrace API (`quantumtrace.api.url`) and the lines around the finding to the API's AI model.
